landing.title: A dialogue language for games
landing.lead: Recite turns plain-text dialogue into checked assets for a game. The runtime returns lines, choices, and typed effect requests; the game decides how to present them and what to do next.
landing.release: This page describes Recite’s v1 scope. Release preparation is still in progress; the installation and distribution guides record what you can use today.
landing.scene.title: At the junction
landing.path.title: From source to game
landing.write.title: Write
landing.write.body: Work in VS Code or VSCodium, Neovim, Zed, or the standalone Recite Writer. The CLI, language server, and workbench use the same project model for diagnostics, stable-ID edits, schema inspection, and preview.
landing.check.title: Check
landing.check.body: Validate source and schema, compile assets, and run scenes against fixtures without opening the game. Traces record the path through a conversation. CI can check that compiled assets still match the files writers edit.
landing.integrate.title: Integrate
landing.integrate.body: Load compiled assets in Bevy, Godot, or Unity. The game answers condition queries, presents dialogue, and carries out effect requests. Recite’s session snapshot records traversal state; your save system keeps it alongside the game state.
landing.localisation.title: Keep the words editable
landing.localisation.body1: Lines and choices have identities separate from their wording. You can revise a sentence without replacing the ID used by a translation or a runtime choice.
landing.localisation.body2: Localisation is optional. When you need it, extract gettext templates with source references and translator context, edit PO catalogues, and test locale and fallback behaviour against the same scene. Recite Writer includes catalogue editing; translation and editorial decisions remain with the people doing that work.
landing.fit.title: Where Recite fits
landing.fit.body1: Recite fits projects that want dialogue in version control, checks outside the engine, and an explicit boundary between narrative source and game code. A project schema describes the conditions, effects, and metadata available to writers.
landing.fit.body2: That boundary takes some integration work. Your game supplies presentation, state, and effect handling. Recite’s workbench is source-first; a general visual node editor is outside v1.
landing.fit.body3: Existing dialogue projects also need a migration review: the importers handle documented subsets, and engine UI, scripts, and saves require separate decisions.

playground.description: Edit the source, then run it locally with Recite’s real compiler and runtime. This preview handles one file; game queries need a host, and effect requests are shown rather than executed.
playground.noJs: Enable JavaScript to run this source. You can still read or download it.
playground.ready: Run the source to start a new scene.
playground.timeout: Execution took too long and was stopped. Edit the source or run again.
playground.failed: The browser runner could not load or execute. Your source is still here; run again to retry.
playground.tooLarge: This preview accepts one source file up to 64 KiB.
playground.changed: Source changed. Run again to start a new scene.
playground.stopped: Execution stopped. Run again to start a new scene.
playground.playing: Continue to the next line or choice.
playground.effect: Effect requested; no game action was performed:
playground.ended: Scene ended. Edit the source or run again.
playground.invalid: The source could not compile. Fix the diagnostics and run again.
playground.downloadTimeout: The compiler download took too long. Check your connection and run again.
playground.resourceLimit: The browser preview stopped during execution. Try reducing the scene or run another file.
